The check normally starts in [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/instrumentation.ts): `register()` runs in the Node.js runtime, loads the event subscribers and calls `startScheduler()`. In [src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts), the scheduler ticks every minute; `tick()` schedules `overdue-issues` on its first tick and then at a 60-minute cadence. It enqueues the job and calls `drain()` in [src/server/jobs/queue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/jobs/queue.ts), whose `runHandler()` calls `runOverdueIssueJob()` with the current time. There is also a direct trigger: `POST` in [src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts) checks the `x-taskflow-cron` secret and invokes the same job.

`runOverdueIssueJob()` in [src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts) wraps its work in `runJob()` for result counts and timing. It first confirms the archive scope filters archived issues, converts the supplied time to an ISO timestamp, and asks `listOrgIdsForRollup(50)` in [src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts) for up to 50 organizations with usage rows, ordered by oldest measurement. For each, `listOverdueIssues()` in [src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts) selects issues in that organization that are unarchived, have a non-null `dueAt` strictly earlier than the check time, and have status `backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, or `in_review`. It returns them ordered by due date. Assignment is not a selection criterion.

For each result, the job emits `issue.overdue` with the organization, issue, project, due date, nullable assignee, check time and a null actor. It announces the domain event; it does not choose recipients, write notification rows or send mail. The module-level `reported` set records the issue ID after `emit()` resolves, so later sweeps in the same process skip it. This is **process-local deduplication**, not a durable exactly-once guarantee: a restart or another process has a separate set, and overlapping runs can both pass the check before either adds the ID. Also, [src/lib/event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/lib/event-bus.ts) isolates subscriber failures: `emit()` waits for handlers but reports their errors without rethrowing them. The job can therefore mark an issue reported even if a notification subscriber failed, or if no subscriber was present.

At startup, importing [src/server/services/event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) loads [src/server/services/notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/services/notification-service.ts), whose module-level `registerFanOut()` subscribes to `issue.overdue`. That handler does nothing for an unassigned issue. Otherwise it calls `notify()` with exactly the assignee ID, kind `issue_overdue`, an overdue title and body, and a link to the issue.

`notify()` looks up that user’s preference for this organization and notification kind using `getPreference()` in [src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts). With no preference row, `resolveChannels()` defaults to `in_app` and `email`. With a row, it includes `in_app` when enabled and includes `email` when enabled and either `digestOnly` is false or the organization’s `digest_email` flag is enabled. If no channels remain, it creates no row. Otherwise `insertNotifications()` in [src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts) stores an unread row addressed to that recipient with the selected channel metadata. The inbox page calls `listNotifications()` for the signed-in actor; the service checks organization scope and permission, and the repository filters by both organization and recipient.

There are limits to the channel behavior in the current implementation. Recording an `email` channel does not itself send an immediate overdue email. The separate `runDigestEmailJob()` in [src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) can build a digest for users with at least one `digestOnly` preference, during the organization’s configured UTC hour and when its digest flag is enabled. `buildDigest()` in [src/server/services/digest-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/services/digest-service.ts) collects their unread rows in the window, and the job marks included rows read after calling `sendEmail()`. That function in [src/server/services/email-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/19bb0b51-940a-4447-b66c-bb4360276d15/src/server/services/email-service.ts) logs email metadata; it has no outbound mail transport. The inbox query and digest builder also do not filter rows by their stored channels, so the selected channel metadata is not fully enforced at those later stages.
